rulings.docket_item: RESPAN PROPOSAL (peer 02, peer_02_r2.json P02-015/P02-016): the tsor-teudah / torah bracket argues the unit may run through MT 8:20.
rulings.decision: DECLINE adoption. The rear seam holds at web:Isa.8.18|web:Isa.8.19; P02-015 stays Isa.8.11-Isa.8.18 and P02-016 stays Isa.8.19-Isa.8.22. The peer-ordered disclosure cure issues instead, with the controlling count-object corrected and one added symmetric disclosure.
rulings.grounds: 1. THE PAIRING IS REAL BUT ITS TIER IS NOT WHAT THE PROPOSAL ASSUMES, and the controlling count objects must be named. The two runs re-splice and re-collate at byte tier: “צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה” (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier) and “לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה” (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier), the same two nouns reversed. But at BYTE tier the absolute testimony noun “תְּעוּדָ֑ה” (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier) stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse, MT 8:16), and the MT 8:20 member is the prefixed “וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה” (oshb:Isa.8.20, byte tier), likewise byte-unique to its own verse (sweep: 1 verse). The two meet only at CONSONANTAL-SKELETON tier, where the noun stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT 8:16 and MT 8:20). Its partner, the absolute “תּוֹרָ֖ה” (oshb:Isa.8.16, byte tier), stands in 2 verses at byte tier (sweep: 2 verses, MT 8:16 and MT 42:21) and 5 at skeleton (sweep: 5 verses, MT 2:3, 8:16, 8:20, 42:21, 51:4) — so the '5 verses' digit both packets carried, and which the peer refined as a spelling-scoped sweep, is controlled by a SKELETON substring object, not by a count of the noun. CONTROLLING OBJECT AND DIGIT PAIR for the whole finding: word-level consonantal skeleton, 2 verses (MT 8:16, MT 8:20). The straddle is therefore a skeleton-tier chiastic echo — citation/mention grade under the tier standard — not a byte-identical device, and a skeleton-tier echo does not outweigh a tier-1 signal at the seam it crosses. 2. THE STANDING SEAM CARRIES AN EXPLICIT TIER-1 SIGNAL THAT SURVIVES SCRUTINY. MT 8:19 opens “וְכִֽי יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם” (oshb:Isa.8.19, byte tier), whose second-person plural addressee element “אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם” (oshb:Isa.8.19, byte tier) is explicit in the bytes, against the first-person prophetic testimony opening MT 8:18, “הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִ֗י” (oshb:Isa.8.18, byte tier). An addressee shift explicit in the bytes is tier-1 under the evidence policy, and the peer round already so held. 3. THE PROPOSAL'S OWN EVIDENCE DOES NOT CARRY THE PROPOSED SPAN. The bracket's opening member stands at MT 8:16, five verses inside a span whose front is the divine-frame formula opening “כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה” (oshb:Isa.8.11, byte tier) at MT 8:11. Read as an inclusio the bracket would delimit MT 8:16-8:20 and would require a SECOND cut at MT 8:15|8:16 — the cut this row itself examined and set aside because the hand-off from quoted divine speech to the prophet's own voice is unmarked in the bytes. Nothing in the peer record disturbs that finding, so the bracket cannot deliver the span it is offered for. 4. SYMMETRY TEST, and it is decisive: relocating the seam to MT 8:20|8:21 does not reduce cross-seam cohesion, it relocates it at the SAME tier. “אֱלֹהָ֣יו” (oshb:Isa.8.19, byte tier; byte-unique to that verse) collates against MT 8:21's bytes at SKELETON tier through “וּבֵאלֹהָ֖יו” (oshb:Isa.8.21, byte tier; byte-unique to that verse), and MT 8:21 opens “וְעָ֥בַר בָּ֖הּ נִקְשֶׁ֣ה וְרָעֵ֑ב” (oshb:Isa.8.21, byte tier), a fresh third-masculine-singular participant against the second-plural address of MT 8:19-8:20. Trading a skeleton-tier straddle at one seam for a skeleton-tier straddle at another is not a gain. 5. TIER-3, PRESENCE ONLY: the WLC parashah layer places SAMEKH at MT 8:18, at the standing seam (single-witness, Prophets tier-3, weak, never a driver). The chapter's marks stand at MT 8:4, 8:8, 8:10, 8:15 and 8:18 only. No use is made of the absence of a mark at MT 8:20 — marker absence is never counterevidence.

consequence.spec: SEAM-PAIR CURE — ONE formulation drafted once and installed on BOTH rows' seam-facing prose; no span, unit_type or parent changes anywhere. (a) P02-015 device_notes AND P02-016 device_notes (the shared formulation): splice “צ֖וֹר תְּעוּדָ֑ה חֲת֥וֹם תּוֹרָ֖ה” (oshb:Isa.8.16) and “לְתוֹרָ֖ה וְלִתְעוּדָ֑ה” (oshb:Isa.8.20), state that the pairing straddles the seam between these two rows, and NAME THE CONTROLLING OBJECT AND TIER exactly: word-level consonantal skeleton, sweep 2 verses book-wide (MT 8:16, MT 8:20); add that at byte tier neither member recurs — the absolute form is byte-unique to MT 8:16 (sweep: 1 verse) and the prefixed form byte-unique to MT 8:20 (sweep: 1 verse) — and that the companion 5-verse digit for the other noun is a skeleton-substring sweep (MT 2:3, 8:16, 8:20, 42:21, 51:4) whose byte-tier count is 2 (MT 8:16, MT 42:21). Then state why the echo does not move the seam. (b) SAME shared formulation, added by this ruling: disclose the symmetric skeleton-tier straddle at the seam the proposal would have created — “אֱלֹהָ֣יו” (oshb:Isa.8.19) against “וּבֵאלֹהָ֖יו” (oshb:Isa.8.21), collating at skeleton tier — and record that the respan was declined because it relocates rather than removes cross-seam cohesion. (c) P02-015 device_notes: name the two distinct objects on the shared consonantal string by splice, “וּלְצ֨וּר מִכְשׁ֜וֹל” (oshb:Isa.8.14, byte tier) against the differently-pointed token opening MT 8:16, rather than in English. (d) P02-015 boundary_rationale: note that the front-seam run opens on the subordinating particle in “כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה” (oshb:Isa.8.11) and say why it is still read as an onset. (e) P02-016 boundary_rationale: replace the bare topic-shift ground with the byte ground present — splice “וְכִֽי יֹאמְר֣וּ אֲלֵיכֶ֗ם” (oshb:Isa.8.19) and argue the front seam from the explicit second-person plural addressee against the first-person testimony of MT 8:18 — and DELETE the range-administration clause ('the last verse of this part's assigned range'), re-arguing the rear seam from the text or lowering confidence accordingly. (f) P02-016: keep the zone-A dual-cite as written (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1), verified correct and on the right content. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS — the tests that killed the original: (i) a cross-seam device sweep over the shared seam must return the pairing AND find it disclosed in both rows' prose in the same words; (ii) every recurrence digit must name its count object and its tier, and the teudah digit must not be stated at byte tier; (iii) the register sweep must find no range-administration or file-order language anywhere in row prose; (iv) the front-seam sentence must cite the addressee element, not a topic label; (v) every added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier against its cited verse with a clean tools\normalize_hebrew_in_json.py dry-run; (vi) every zone-A ref keeps its dual.

rulings.docket_item: RESPAN PROPOSAL (peer 08, peer_08.json P10-005): close the unit at Isa.36.22 and open the next at Isa.37.1; LF's rival variant carries 37:1 forward with Hezekiah's response.
rulings.decision: ADOPT. The two recorded variants are one operation seen from two sides and are adopted together: web:Isa.37.1 leaves P10-005 and opens P10-006, which then runs web:Isa.37.1-Isa.37.7 with Hezekiah's response arc intact.
rulings.grounds: NARRATIVE-ZONE LAW APPLIED, not reinterpreted. 1. THE ADOPTED SEAM IS A SCENE-AND-PARTICIPANT SEAM, tier-1. MT 36:22 closes with the delegation as acting subject, “וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ” (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte tier). MT 37:1 opens “וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ” (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte tier) — a verse-initial wayehi plus temporal infinitive clause plus an EXPLICIT new grammatical subject, and the acting subject changes from the delegation to the king across the junction. Object named: verse-initial wayehi (first token, consonantal skeleton, exact token match) stands at exactly 7 verses book-wide (sweep: 7 verses — MT 7:1, 22:7, 36:1, 37:1, 37:38, 38:4, 48:19), of which 4 fall in the N4 narrative zone (MT 36:1, 37:1, 37:38, 38:4). Only MT 36:1 and MT 37:1 pair it with a temporal frame AND an explicit new subject: “וַיְהִ֡י בְּאַרְבַּע֩” (oshb:Isa.36.1, byte tier) and “וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ”; MT 37:38's “וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה” (oshb:Isa.37.38, byte tier) is an independent pronoun plus participle with the subject unchanged, and MT 38:4's “וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה” (oshb:Isa.38.4, byte tier) is the word-event noun phrase. MT 36:1 is the parent frame's own onset under the 8-frame architecture, so the construction at MT 37:1 is the same discourse-frame scene onset the block itself opens with. 2. THE STANDING SEAM HAS NO SUCH WARRANT AND CUTS A CONTINUOUS CLAUSE. MT 37:2 opens “וַ֠יִּשְׁלַח” (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte tier) with Hezekiah still the subject, and “וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק” (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte tier) is picked up immediately by “מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים” (oshb:Isa.37.2, byte tier) — same verbal root in a different stem plus the same noun pluralized: ROOT tier, NOT byte-identical recurrence. The drafted bound cuts between two clauses sharing both subject and device; the adopted bound does not. 3. THE COUNTER-DEVICE IS REAL, WEAKER, AND SURVIVES AS A DISCLOSURE. “קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים” (oshb:Isa.36.22, byte tier) is answered across the adopted seam by “וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו” (oshb:Isa.37.1, byte tier): shared root, distinct pointed forms — ROOT tier, not byte-identical. Under 'frame + speech = default larger unit' a root-tier report-and-response tie does not outweigh a scene-onset frame plus a subject shift; it becomes cross-seam disclosure on the adopted seam, not a veto. 4. TIER-3, PRESENCE ONLY: the sole PE or SAMEKH inside MT 36:21-37:1 is the SAMEKH at MT 36:22, which under the drafted span sat at the row's own internal join and under the adopted span falls at the seam. Single-witness, Prophets tier-3, weak, never a driver; it corroborates and drives nothing, and no absence is used. 5. The 2 Kgs 18-20 parallel is not consulted and decides nothing here.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED SPAN SET — exact: P10-005 span becomes "Isa.36.21-Isa.36.22", unit_type narrative_prose (unchanged), parent_collection "N4 Isa.36.1-Isa.39.8" (unchanged). P10-006 span becomes "Isa.37.1-Isa.37.7", unit_type narrative_prose (unchanged), parent_collection "N4 Isa.36.1-Isa.39.8" (unchanged). No row is created or retired; chunk_index_in_book is unchanged for every row in the book. TILING CONSEQUENCE: 3 + 6 verses becomes 2 + 7; check_tiling.py --range Isa.1.1-Isa.66.24 returns verses_covered 1292 of 1292 expected over 225 decisions, GREEN (simulated and verified). SIDE EFFECT TO RECORD: P10-005 ceases to be a chapter-straddling span, leaving three straddles in the corpus (P01-015, P16-002, P18-003). No 8-frame seam is touched — 35:10|36:1 and 39:8|40:1 both stand. P10-005 AUTHOR WORK, every field enumerated: (1) span as above. (2) boundary_rationale: delete the whole chapter-crossing argument ('the same participants and the same report-and-response movement', 'chapter divisions never cutting on their own authority') — it is now false of this row — and re-argue the close from the delegation-as-subject clause, splicing “וַיַּגִּ֣ידוּ ל֔וֹ” (oshb:Isa.36.22) with its tier. (3) device_notes: replace the chapter-span note with the cross-seam disclosure of the tear-and-garment pair — “קְרוּעֵ֣י בְגָדִ֑ים” (oshb:Isa.36.22) against “וַיִּקְרַ֖ע אֶת בְּגָדָ֑יו” (oshb:Isa.37.1) — NAMED AS ROOT TIER, not byte-identical; this is a SEAM-PAIR disclosure, ONE formulation shared with P10-006. (4) device_notes or boundary_rationale: restate the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.36.22 as tier-3 single-witness corroboration OF THE ADOPTED SEAM (weak, never a driver, absence never counterevidence), not as a mark inside the span. (5) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut to carry the rival this ruling DECLINED — that MT 37:1 closes the officials' report — and say what defeats it (scene-onset frame plus subject shift). (6) boundary_evidence_refs: drop web:Isa.37.1 and oshb:Isa.37.1 as in-span refs and re-add oshb:Isa.37.1 as a cross-seam ref; add oshb:Isa.36.22. (7) confidence and observed_substrate_signals re-open: the row is now a two-verse scene-closure unit; re-derive rather than carry 'medium' forward. P10-006 AUTHOR WORK, every field enumerated: (1) span as above. (2) boundary_rationale: prepend the onset argument — splice “וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ חִזְקִיָּ֔הוּ” (oshb:Isa.37.1) with its tier, name the verse-initial wayehi object and its digits (7 verses book-wide, 4 in the N4 zone, 2 with an explicit new subject), and argue the participant shift from the delegation to the king. (3) device_notes: the covering-in-sackcloth tie “וַיִּתְכַּ֣ס בַּשָּׂ֔ק” (oshb:Isa.37.1) to “מִתְכַּסִּ֖ים בַּשַּׂקִּ֑ים” (oshb:Isa.37.2) is now INTERNAL to this row — restate it as internal cohesion evidence FOR the adopted span at ROOT tier; do not delete it and do not leave it labelled a cross-seam tie. (4) device_notes: carry the shared seam-pair tear-and-garment formulation from P10-005, identically worded. (5) strongest_rejected_alternative: keep the MT 37:5 rival and ADD the rear rival that MT 37:1 belongs with the officials' report. (6) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Isa.37.1, oshb:Isa.37.2, oshb:Isa.36.22. (7) confidence re-opens — 'high' was recorded for a differently-bounded unit and must be re-derived. (8) COMPOSITION NOTICE: peer_08.json ruling P10-006 already orders a device_notes digit repair on this same row (Assyrian king owns THREE prior royal-messenger koh-amar sites, MT 36:4, 36:14, 36:16, of a 4-verse royal-messenger set against 44 divine-frame verses; the Judahite frame at MT 37:3 is the fourth SITE and the second frame-OWNER; and the prefixed speech-commission inside oshb:Isa.37.6 must be distinguished from the counted frame). That remedy is UNDISTURBED by this respan and must ship in the SAME author pass — it is not superseded and must not be dropped. TESTS THE ADOPTION MUST PASS — the tests that killed the original: (i) the cross-seam cohesion sweep over BOTH rows' seams must find every byte-true or root-true device disclosed with its tier, and must find the sackcloth tie relabelled as internal; (ii) a subject scan across MT 36:21-37:7 must agree with every participant claim either row makes; (iii) no row prose may argue a bound from a chapter division; (iv) check_tiling.py returns 1292/1292 GREEN; (v) every Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run.

rulings.docket_item: RESPAN PROPOSAL (peer 13, peer_13.json P15-002/P15-003, with P15-001 front context from peer_12_r2.json): hold web:Isa.53.1-Isa.53.12 undivided.
rulings.decision: ADOPT. web:Isa.53.1-Isa.53.12 is held undivided as one unit; the person-shift cut at web:Isa.53.9|web:Isa.53.10 is withdrawn. The servant referent stays undecided, as it does under every outcome, and nothing here decides it.
rulings.grounds: 1. THE SEAM'S STATED DRIVER DOES NOT DISCRIMINATE THE SEAM. “וַיהוָ֞ה חָפֵ֤ץ דַּכְּאוֹ֙” (oshb:Isa.53.10, byte tier) opens MT 53:10, and its opening token is byte-unique to that verse (sweep: 1 verse at byte tier). Its partner “וַֽיהוָה֙ הִפְגִּ֣יעַ” (oshb:Isa.53.6, byte tier) stands MID-VERSE inside the very row the seam is supposed to close. The two meet at SKELETON tier only — sweep: 5 verses book-wide (MT 3:17, 31:3, 53:6, 53:10, 58:9), accent-stripped 3 verses (MT 3:17, 53:10, 58:9), byte 1 verse. CONTROLLING OBJECT AND DIGIT PAIR: consonantal skeleton, 5 verses; MT 53:6 and MT 53:10 are its only in-chapter pair. A construction the row carries on BOTH sides of its own seam cannot mark it. 2. THE RESIDUAL WARRANT — 'the turn to the divine agent' — IS NOT IN THE BYTES EITHER, and this is the finding that decides the item. The divine agent is ALREADY acting inside the span at MT 53:6, in that same “וַֽיהוָה֙ הִפְגִּ֣יעַ” clause, so MT 53:10 is a return, not a turn. And a first-person-singular possessive already stands inside the span at MT 53:8, “עַמִּ֖י” (oshb:Isa.53.8, byte tier; that pointed form in 11 verses book-wide) — recorded WITHOUT deciding whose first-person voice it is, the referent staying undecided. From the other side, the communal voice the row names as its own criterion stops at “כֻּלָּֽנוּ” (oshb:Isa.53.6, byte tier), three verses before the cut, as the row's own device_notes concedes. Neither voice partitions at MT 53:9|53:10. What is left at the seam is verse-initial position alone, and verse-initial position is not a tier-1 signal. Under the owner-gate rule that internal rows cut only at tier-1 seams, this cut has no ground left. 3. POSITIVELY, A BYTE-IDENTICAL BRACKET STRADDLES THE WITHDRAWN SEAM. “נָשָׂ֔א” spliced from oshb:Isa.53.4 is BYTE-IDENTICAL to “נָשָׂ֔א” spliced from oshb:Isa.53.12 and stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide at BYTE tier (sweep: 2 verses, MT 53:4 and MT 53:12; accent-stripped 6 verses; skeleton 39 verses — the skeleton digit is a substring object and is not the one cited). Both members fall inside the merged span, one on each side of the withdrawn cut. Byte-tier is quotation grade; this is the strongest device in the passage and it argues continuity across the cut. 4. THE MERGED SPAN'S FRONT IS INDEPENDENTLY WARRANTED AND IS NOT RE-OPENED. “לִשְׁמֻעָתֵ֑נוּ” (oshb:Isa.53.1, byte tier; byte-unique at every tier) carries the first-person plural against the third person closing MT 52:15 — the seam already adjudicated at P15-001's rear edge and left standing. So the bracket is not being asked to define the unit's front, only to defeat an internal cut it straddles. 5. THE CLOSE IS UNCHANGED AND INDEPENDENTLY WARRANTED: the divine first-person verb “לָכֵ֞ן אֲחַלֶּק” (oshb:Isa.53.12, byte tier) closes, and MT 54:1 opens a fresh vocative imperative to a new addressee. TIER-3, PRESENCE ONLY: the WLC layer places SAMEKH at MT 53:12, the merged unit's own close, and at MT 52:12 before the song's announcement (single-witness, weak, never a driver). No use is made of the absence of a mark at MT 53:9. 6. HELD CLASSIC PRESERVED: the servant referent is not decided, not narrowed, and not implied by this bound.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED SPAN SET — exact: P15-002 span becomes "Isa.53.1-Isa.53.12", unit_type servant_song (unchanged), parent_collection "M6 Isa.49.1-Isa.55.13" (unchanged), confidence medium_low, frontier_flag_considered true. P15-003 is RETIRED as a decision row, its content merged into P15-002 with a retirement note naming this ruling. TILING CONSEQUENCE: 9 + 3 verses becomes 12; the book drops one decision row. check_tiling.py --range Isa.1.1-Isa.66.24 returns 1292 of 1292 GREEN (simulated and verified, jointly with B-2 and B-5, at 223 decisions). RENUMBER: chunk_index_in_book must be re-sequenced for every row after the merged row — P15-004 and all following rows shift down by one. P15-001 and P15-004 are listed here ONLY as renumber/neighbour consequences: P15-001's rear-seam prose and its own peer remedy (peer_12_r2.json) are untouched by this ruling, and P15-004's span web:Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 is unchanged. CLASS INTERACTION, MANDATORY: web:Isa.53.1-Isa.53.12 IS A WHOLE-CHAPTER SPAN (WEB Isa 53 = 12 verses, verse_inventory.json). On adoption the merged row ENROLS in the whole-chapter class ruled at B-6 — confidence capped at medium_low, the cap disclosed in prose, frontier_flag_considered true, and the full low-band machinery applied. This is the companion consequence most likely to be missed. MERGED-ROW AUTHOR WORK, every field enumerated: (1) span, confidence and frontier flag as above. (2) boundary_rationale: delete the internal-seam argument in both source rows — the subject-fronted divine-name pivot no longer bounds anything — and re-argue only the two outer seams (the first-person-plural onset at oshb:Isa.53.1 against MT 52:15; the divine first-person close at oshb:Isa.53.12 against the vocative opening MT 54:1). (3) boundary_rationale or device_notes: install the internal bracket as evidence FOR the merged span — splice “נָשָׂ֔א” (oshb:Isa.53.4) and “נָשָׂ֔א” (oshb:Isa.53.12), name BYTE tier and the digit (sweep: 2 verses book-wide), and state that it is what defeated the internal cut. The peer's cross-seam disclosure order on this pair is NOT dropped — it is restated as internal. (4) device_notes: record the two byte facts that defeated the voice partition — the divine agent already acting at MT 53:6 and the first-person-singular possessive “עַמִּ֖י” at oshb:Isa.53.8 (byte tier), with the referent expressly left undecided — and record that the communal pronoun stops at “כֻּלָּֽנוּ” (oshb:Isa.53.6, byte tier). (5) CARRY FORWARD, UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE, the surviving peer remedies: from peer_13.json P15-002 item (b), the quote/gloss parity repair at oshb:Isa.53.6 — the spliced token and the English clause must name the same position, or re-splice the verse-final form; from peer_13.json P15-003 item (a), the servant-possessive tier repair — replace 'recurs' with the collate truth that oshb:Isa.52.13 and oshb:Isa.53.11 are NOT byte-identical and meet at accent-stripped tier, carrying the digits (byte tier: 2 verses each; accent-stripped: 14 verses). Both survive the merge and must ship in this pass. (6) strongest_rejected_alternative: it must now carry the rival this ruling DECLINED — splitting at MT 53:9|53:10 on the verse-initial divine-name clause — argued from the bytes, with the WEB half-verse framing at MT 53:11 deleted per peer_13.json P15-002 item (c) and the rival re-keyed to the MT bytes with a pointed splice. (7) observed_substrate_signals: re-derive for the merged unit; the divine_close_voice and we_report_voice keys of the two source rows cannot both stand unexamined, and the signal that keyed the withdrawn seam must go. (8) device_notes: disclose the SAMEKH at MT 53:12 as tier-3 single-witness corroboration of the close only. (9) The servant referent stays undecided in every field. TESTS THE ADOPTION MUST PASS — the tests that killed the original: (i) collate “נָשָׂ֔א” against oshb:Isa.53.4 and oshb:Isa.53.12 — both must return byte — and re-run the sweep to 2 verses; (ii) a voice/person scan across MT 53:1-53:12 must agree with every person claim the merged row makes, and no partition may be asserted at a verse the scan does not support; (iii) every recurrence claim names its tier and its count object; (iv) no field decides or narrows the servant referent; (v) check_tiling.py returns 1292/1292 GREEN at the re-sequenced row count; (vi) the whole-chapter cap disclosure is present and confidence is medium_low; (vii) clean normalize dry-run.

rulings.docket_item: RESERVED SEAM QUESTION (peer 03, peer_03_r2.json P03-012, cluster c06): whether the one-verse unit web:Isa.11.10 should stand, fold back, or fold forward.
rulings.decision: IT STANDS. P03-012 keeps span Isa.11.10-Isa.11.10; no fold is adopted in either direction. A disclosure cure issues — the peer's evidence-layer remedy, plus the boundary-layer disclosures this ruling adds, since the strongest rival is currently named nowhere in the corpus.
rulings.grounds: 1. THE ROW'S SOLE ONSET DRIVER CANNOT DISCRIMINATE ITS REAR SEAM, and the peer is exactly right on the tier. “וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא” (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) and “וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא” (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) differ ONLY in accents: identical at accent-stripped AND skeleton tier, NOT byte-identical. Digits with objects named: the MT 11:10 run stands at 6 verses book-wide at byte tier (sweep: 6 verses — MT 7:23, 11:10, 17:4, 23:15, 24:21, 27:12) and at 13 verses at accent-stripped and skeleton tier alike (sweep: 13 verses), four of them in this immediate stretch (MT 10:20, 10:27, 11:10, 11:11). A frame both sides of a seam carry cannot mark that seam. 2. BUT THE REAR SEAM IS NOT THEREFORE UNWARRANTED — it is UNDER-ARGUED. MT 11:11 introduces an explicit new agent and marks its own act as a repetition: “יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙” (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier). An agent/participant shift explicit in the bytes is a tier-1 class. The row states this only in English and hangs it on the second-time token, which the peer correctly located as the sixth token of its verse rather than its opener. 3. THE FOLD-BACK IS THE STRONGEST RIVAL AND IT IS NAMED NOWHERE — not in the row, not in either packet, not in the peer ruling. CONTROLLING OBJECT: the Jesse name at WORD-BOUND consonantal skeleton stands at exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, MT 11:1 and MT 11:10) — “יִשָׁ֑י” (oshb:Isa.11.1, byte tier; byte-unique to that verse) against “יִשַׁ֗י” (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier; byte-unique to that verse). HAZARD NAMED: the bare three-letter substring digit for the same name is 22 verses and is a short-token trap — word-bound is the only citable object here. Those two verses are the first and last of the span a fold-back would create (P03-011 + this row), so this is a genuine proper-name inclusio and it is the rival that has to be beaten, not the forward fold the row argues against. 4. THE FOLD-FORWARD IS WEAKER THAN EITHER PACKET PRESENTS IT, and the peer's mis-attachment finding is confirmed and extended. “עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים” (oshb:Isa.11.10, byte tier) is unique at every tier (sweep: 1 verse); “וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם” (oshb:Isa.11.12, byte tier) reaches 2 verses at skeleton (sweep: 2 verses, MT 5:26 and MT 11:12) — a DIFFERENT object from the 11:10-to-11:12 straddle it was adduced for. The two are distinct collocations built on distinct spellings of the banner noun, so the straddle is a root-level observation across two spellings, not a token match; the bare noun word-bound stands at 6 verses (MT 5:26, 11:12, 13:2, 18:3, 33:23, 62:10) and does NOT include MT 11:10, whose form is prefixed, while the bare substring reaches 44 verses — the trap. 5. WHY IT STANDS. Both of the row's seams carry tier-1-eligible grounds: at the front, the in-that-day discourse frame opens MT 11:10 where MT 11:9 has none — and the corpus already treats that same frame as a row onset one verse later at MT 11:11 (P03-013's own front), so declining it here would be inconsistent with a bound this ruling is not asked to disturb; at the rear, the explicit agent shift of item 2. The fold-back inclusio is real but it is word-bound SKELETON tier against a discourse frame plus an agent shift, both tier-1 — not enough to carry a merge. TIER-3, PRESENCE AT BOTH SEAMS: the WLC layer places PE at MT 11:9 and PE at MT 11:10 — the chapter's only two marks — isolating exactly this verse. Single-witness, Prophets tier-3, weak, never a driver, cited as presence only. And the peer's cleanest defect is sustained: no ranking of one paragraph-break type as more emphatic than the other is sourceable from the inventory the row cites, which records type and count only.

consequence.spec: No span, unit_type or parent changes on any of the three rows. P03-012 remains Isa.11.10-Isa.11.10, salvation_oracle, M1 Isa.1.2-Isa.12.6, medium_low with the frontier flag already set. P03-012 AUTHOR WORK: (1) device_notes: DELETE the phrase ranking one paragraph-break type as more emphatic than the other; keep both marks named, typed and unranked, tier-3, single-witness, corroborating only. (2) boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose that the in-that-day frame opening this verse also opens the immediately following verse, naming the tier explicitly (identical at accent-stripped AND skeleton, NOT byte) and both digits with objects (byte 6 verses; accent-stripped and skeleton 13 verses), and state what carries the seam once a frame shared by both sides is set aside. (3) boundary_rationale: re-argue the rear seam from “יוֹסִ֨יף אֲדֹנָ֤י שֵׁנִית֙” (oshb:Isa.11.11, byte tier) as an explicit agent/participant shift — tier-1 class — rather than from the second-time token, whose position the row must state correctly. (4) device_notes: disclose the banner recurrence across the rear seam using the ATTESTED COLLOCATIONS with their own digits and tiers — “עֹמֵד֙ לְנֵ֣ס עַמִּ֔ים” (1 verse, all tiers) and “וְנָשָׂ֥א נֵס֙ לַגּוֹיִ֔ם” (2 verses at skeleton) — and state expressly that the bare banner noun may not be swept (substring 44 verses, word-bound 6 verses not including MT 11:10). (5) strongest_rejected_alternative: REPLACE it. The field currently adjudicates the forward fold; it must instead adjudicate the FOLD-BACK, naming the Jesse inclusio by splice — “יִשָׁ֑י” (oshb:Isa.11.1) against “יִשַׁ֗י” (oshb:Isa.11.10) — at WORD-BOUND consonantal-skeleton tier, sweep 2 verses book-wide, with the 22-verse bare-substring digit expressly rejected as a short-token trap, and must say what defeats it. The forward fold may be kept as a second, weaker rival. SEAM-PAIR MIRRORS — ONE formulation each, drafted once and installed on both sides: (6) P03-011 device_notes carries the SAME Jesse-inclusio disclosure as P03-012 item (5), since that device straddles the P03-011|P03-012 seam and P03-011's rear-facing prose currently ignores it. (7) P03-013 boundary_rationale or device_notes carries the SAME shared-frame disclosure as P03-012 item (2) — that its own onset frame is the accent-variant twin of the preceding row's, identical at accent-stripped and skeleton and not at byte — since P03-013 rests its front seam on that frame; and P03-013 must state what discriminates its onset once the shared frame is set aside. TESTS THE CURE MUST PASS — the tests that killed the original: (i) no formula may drive a cut without a disclosed tier and a stated reason it discriminates the seam it draws; (ii) every recurrence digit names the object it counts, and no digit rests on a bare short-token skeleton; (iii) the rejected-alternative field carries the strongest rival, tested here as the fold-back, not the weaker forward fold; (iv) the cross-seam device sweep over BOTH of P03-012's seams finds nothing undisclosed on either side; (v) no prose ranks parashah types; (vi) every Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier with a clean normalize dry-run.

rulings.docket_item: SHARED-SEAM CONDITIONAL (peer 07, peer_07_r2.json P09-003 and P09-004, cluster c14): whether the web:Isa.32.15|web:Isa.32.16 seam warrants a respan now.
rulings.decision: RESPAN IS WARRANTED NOW ON THE BYTES, and is ADOPTED: the seam at web:Isa.32.15|web:Isa.32.16 is withdrawn and P09-003 and P09-004 merge into one unit, web:Isa.32.9-Isa.32.20. The peer's grounds repairs are folded into the merged row rather than discharged separately. As the peer stated, this lands on both rows as ONE decision.
rulings.grounds: 1. NEITHER SIDE OF THE SEAM SUPPLIES A LAWFUL GROUND, and this is established, not inferred. P09-003's rear-edge criterion is that two verses 'form one sentence in the WEB rendering', repeated in its own strongest_rejected_alternative — modern sentence punctuation is tier-4 metadata and is NEVER boundary evidence. P09-004's ONLY stated boundary ground is a register change, and the bytes locate it at the wrong verse: the last second-person forms in the stretch are “חִרְדוּ֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.11, byte tier) and the imperatives following them — four verses ahead of the cut the claim is used to justify. So one side argues from a forbidden criterion and the other from a byte-false location. 2. NO TIER-1 SEAM EXISTS AT MT 32:15|32:16. MT 32:15 opens the subordinating “עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה” (oshb:Isa.32.15, byte tier), which binds BACK to the desolation of MT 32:14 rather than opening anything; MT 32:16 opens “וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט” (oshb:Isa.32.16, byte tier), a waw-plus-perfect continuing that same clause; and the chain runs on unbroken through MT 32:17, MT 32:18 and MT 32:19 with no verse-initial marker, no vocative, no frame formula and no participant change at any point. Under the owner-gate rule that internal rows cut only at tier-1 seams, this cut has nothing to stand on — and P09-003's own criterion, applied consistently, reads straight past its own close. 3. THE MERGED UNIT'S OUTER SEAMS BOTH DO. FRONT: MT 32:9 opens “נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י” (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte tier) — a vocative plus second-person feminine plural imperatives, tier-1 — against the third-person description of MT 32:1-32:8, with PE at MT 32:8 as tier-3 presence corroboration. REAR: the beatitude “אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם” (oshb:Isa.32.20, byte tier) closes, SAMEKH stands at MT 32:20 (tier-3 presence), and MT 33:1 opens “ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד” (oshb:Isa.33.1, byte tier) — a woe header, which under the owner-gate architecture bounds the parent oracle. Both outer seams are already the drafted corpus's own bounds and are unchanged by this ruling. 4. POSITIVELY, THE MERGED SPAN IS BRACKETED BY ITS OWN CHAIN, and the peer's digit and tier both re-derive exactly. “שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.9, byte tier) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to “שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.11, byte tier) — sweep: 2 verses at byte tier — and “שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.18, byte tier) joins them at CONSONANTAL-SKELETON tier only, giving exactly 3 verses book-wide at that tier (sweep: 3 verses, MT 32:9, 32:11, 32:18) and nowhere else in Isaiah. The chain's outer members are the merged unit's onset verse (second word of MT 32:9) and the final word of MT 32:18. Unlike the bracket declined at B-1, this one's opening member IS the proposed unit's first verse, so it delimits the span it is offered for. 5. TESTED AND REJECTED AS UNUSABLE, stated so no author re-adopts it: the eternity phrase at MT 32:14 and MT 32:17 is NOT a cross-seam device — the two forms are not byte-identical and meet only at skeleton, where the form stands at 41 verses book-wide. It is not cited and must not be. 6. Every tier-3 citation above is presence, single-witness, weak and never a driver; the absence of any parashah mark inside MT 32:9-32:19 is disclosed nowhere as evidence and carries no weight either way.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED SPAN SET — exact: P09-003 span becomes "Isa.32.9-Isa.32.20", unit_type judgment_oracle (unchanged from P09-003), parent_collection "M3 Isa.28.1-Isa.35.10" (unchanged), confidence medium_low, frontier_flag_considered true. P09-004 is RETIRED as a decision row, its content merged into P09-003 with a retirement note naming this ruling. UNIT_TYPE JUSTIFIED UNDER THE OPERATIVE-CATEGORY LAW: the merged row's own bytes carry a vocative judgment address at its onset (“נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י”, oshb:Isa.32.9, byte tier) governing the whole; the restoration arrives INSIDE it as the resolution of the subordinating clause at MT 32:15 and closes in a beatitude. judgment_oracle therefore applies on the row's own bytes, and the row must carry the one-sentence deviation disclosure naming the restoration turn and the beatitude close. The 10-value vocabulary is not extended. TILING CONSEQUENCE: 7 + 5 verses becomes 12; the book drops one decision row. check_tiling.py --range Isa.1.1-Isa.66.24 returns 1292 of 1292 GREEN (simulated and verified jointly with B-2 and B-3 at 223 decisions). RENUMBER: chunk_index_in_book must be re-sequenced for every row after the merged row. NOT a whole-chapter span (WEB Isa 32 = 20 verses; the span starts at 32:9), so the B-6 cap does not attach — but medium_low lands in the low band, so the low-band machinery of B-6 DOES apply to this row. MERGED-ROW AUTHOR WORK, every field enumerated: (1) span, unit_type, confidence and frontier flag as above. (2) boundary_rationale: STRIKE from both source rows' text the one-sentence-in-the-English criterion (it appears in P09-003's boundary_rationale AND its strongest_rejected_alternative) and STRIKE P09-004's claim that the second-person plural address drops after Isa.32.15 — that sentence is byte-false as written and cannot be reworded, only replaced. (3) boundary_rationale: argue the two surviving outer seams from spliced pointed forms with tiers named — the onset “נָשִׁים֙ שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת קֹ֖מְנָה שְׁמַ֣עְנָה קוֹלִ֑י” (oshb:Isa.32.9), the beatitude close “אַשְׁרֵיכֶ֕ם” (oshb:Isa.32.20), and the woe header “ה֣וֹי שׁוֹדֵ֗ד” (oshb:Isa.33.1) bounding the far side. (4) boundary_rationale or device_notes: install the internal clause chain as evidence FOR the merged span — splice “עַד יֵ֨עָרֶ֥ה” (oshb:Isa.32.15) and “וְשָׁכַ֥ן בַּמִּדְבָּ֖ר מִשְׁפָּ֑ט” (oshb:Isa.32.16), name the waw-plus-perfect continuation, and state that this is what withdrew the seam; and record that the English adverb rendering MT 32:16 renders that waw form, the Hebrew adverb's 6 verse-initial sites not including this verse. (5) device_notes: install the bracket — “שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.9) and “שַֽׁאֲנַנּ֔וֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.11) at BYTE tier, “שַׁאֲנַנּֽוֹת” (oshb:Isa.32.18) at consonantal-skeleton tier, sweep 3 verses book-wide — plus the root-level answer of the trust forms into MT 32:18 with its digits and tiers named as root-level across distinct attested spellings, never as a token match. (6) strongest_rejected_alternative: it must now carry the rival this ruling DECLINED — cutting at MT 32:15|32:16 — argued from the bytes, with the tier-4 punctuation criterion and the byte-false register claim both absent. (7) observed_substrate_signals: P09-004's topic-onset key is falsified and its blessing-formula key is unevidenced in Hebrew; P09-003's addressee-shift key survives for the onset only. Re-derive the whole list for the merged unit. (8) device_notes: keep P09-003's ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Isa.32.15 (single-witness apparatus, disclosed without adjudicating the reading) and keep the PE at MT 32:8 and SAMEKH at MT 32:20 as tier-3 presence corroboration of the outer seams only. (9) boundary_evidence_refs: add oshb:Isa.32.9, oshb:Isa.32.11, oshb:Isa.32.15, oshb:Isa.32.16, oshb:Isa.32.18, oshb:Isa.32.20 and oshb:Isa.33.1. (10) The outpoured-spirit referent stays a live construal question and is not decided. TESTS THE ADOPTION MUST PASS — the tests that killed the original: (i) a person-form scan across MT 32:9-32:20 must agree with every person claim the merged row makes, and no ground may be asserted at a verse the scan does not support; (ii) with every appeal to the English rendering and its punctuation deleted, both outer seams must still stand on spliced pointed forms with named tiers; (iii) no criterion may be stated that, applied consistently, would carry the unit past its own close; (iv) every recurrence digit names its tier and count object, and the eternity phrase is not cited as a device; (v) check_tiling.py returns 1292/1292 GREEN at the re-sequenced row count; (vi) clean normalize dry-run.

rulings.docket_item: CLASS DISPOSITION: the whole-chapter confidence-cap class — P02-009, P04-008, P09-001, P09-006, P09-007, P17-001.
rulings.decision: The one-pass author treatment is CONFIRMED for all six docketed rows, and the CLASS ENUMERATION IS CORRECTED: the class is not six rows but twelve, of which TEN sit above the medium_low cap. Four cap violations — P03-014, P05-005, P05-009, P16-005 — appear in no packet, no peer ruling and no docket line, and would ship above the cap if the class shipped as six.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived deterministically by sweeping every row's span against the chapter verse counts in SP\Isa\verse_inventory.json (1292 verses over 66 chapters; check_tiling GREEN at 1292/1292). THE SIX DOCKETED ROWS ALL VERIFY AS EXACT WHOLE-CHAPTER SPANS AND ALL SIT ABOVE THE CAP: P02-009 Isa.6.1-Isa.6.13 (ch 6 = 13 verses) at high; P04-008 Isa.15.1-Isa.15.9 (ch 15 = 9) at high; P09-001 Isa.31.1-Isa.31.9 (ch 31 = 9) at medium; P09-006 Isa.34.1-Isa.34.17 (ch 34 = 17) at high; P09-007 Isa.35.1-Isa.35.10 (ch 35 = 10) at high; P17-001 Isa.60.1-Isa.60.22 (ch 60 = 22) at high. The peers' cap drops to medium_low on all six are confirmed and adopted. FOUR MORE ARE EQUALLY WHOLE-CHAPTER AND EQUALLY ABOVE THE CAP AND ARE UNLISTED ANYWHERE: P03-014 Isa.12.1-Isa.12.6 (ch 12 = 6 verses) at high; P05-005 Isa.18.1-Isa.18.7 (ch 18 = 7) at high; P05-009 Isa.20.1-Isa.20.6 (ch 20 = 6) at medium; P16-005 Isa.58.1-Isa.58.14 (ch 58 = 14) at medium. TWO MORE ARE WHOLE-CHAPTER AND ALREADY AT THE CAP, needing the disclosure and the machinery check but no drop: P09-005 Isa.33.1-Isa.33.24 (ch 33 = 24) at medium_low; P15-004 Isa.54.1-Isa.54.17 (ch 54 = 17) at medium_low. WHY THE FOUR SLIPPED, and this is the durability point: the shipped validator suite does not mechanize the cap at all. SP\Isa\draft_rows_combined.jsonl.validator_report.json contains no cap gate, no confidence check and no whole-chapter check — its hard_status is GREEN with 151 triage flags while ten cap violations stand. A rule enforced only by reviewer attention will be enumerated short every time, so repair symmetry here has to be a sweep against the verse inventory, not a list carried forward from the packets. FRONTIER FLAGS, re-derived: nine of the twelve carry frontier_flag_considered = false (P02-009, P03-014, P04-008, P05-005, P05-009, P09-006, P09-007, P16-005, P17-001); three already carry true (P09-001, P09-005, P15-004). CLASS INTERACTION: adopting B-3 creates a THIRTEENTH whole-chapter row, web:Isa.53.1-Isa.53.12 (ch 53 = 12 verses), which enrols in this class on adoption at medium_low.

consequence.spec: ONE author pass over the whole class; no span, unit_type or parent changes anywhere — this is a confidence-and-machinery disposition only. GROUP A — TEN ROWS ABOVE THE CAP, confidence set to medium_low: P02-009 (from high), P03-014 (from high), P04-008 (from high), P05-005 (from high), P05-009 (from medium), P09-001 (from medium), P09-006 (from high), P09-007 (from high), P16-005 (from medium), P17-001 (from high). GROUP B — TWO ROWS ALREADY AT THE CAP, confidence unchanged, everything else in this spec still applies: P09-005, P15-004. GROUP C — ONE ROW ON ADOPTION OF B-3: the merged P15-002 at web:Isa.53.1-Isa.53.12, set at medium_low by that ruling and enrolled here. FOR EVERY ROW IN ALL THREE GROUPS: (1) confidence as above. (2) frontier_flag_considered set to true — required on the nine currently false (P02-009, P03-014, P04-008, P05-005, P05-009, P09-006, P09-007, P16-005, P17-001) and verified already true on the rest. (3) FULL LOW-BAND MACHINERY, since medium_low is in the low band: three-sidecar mirroring installed, and a frontier-queue row raised for each. (4) A one-sentence cap disclosure in the row's own prose naming the span as whole-chapter, naming the chapter's verse count from verse_inventory.json, and stating that the confidence is capped by the campaign rule rather than lowered by a new defect — so that a later reader cannot mistake the cap for an evidence finding. (5) No boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative or device_notes content is deleted by this disposition; where a peer ruling independently orders repairs on one of these rows, those repairs ship in the SAME pass and are not superseded. TEST THE CURE MUST PASS — the test that caught the four unlisted rows: re-run the whole-chapter sweep (every row span compared against SP\Isa\verse_inventory.json chapter counts) and require that the returned set of exact whole-chapter rows be IDENTICAL to the treated set, with every member at confidence medium_low or lower, frontier_flag_considered true, low-band machinery present, and the cap disclosure in prose. A treated list that is shorter than the swept list fails. Additionally: check_tiling.py must still return 1292/1292 GREEN, and the pass must not alter any span.

rulings.docket_item: CLASS DISPOSITION: the P05 NFD-degraded-quote class (23 pointed-Hebrew quotes, boundary_rationale fields), docketed as 11 rows P05-001..P05-011.
rulings.decision: The deterministic class-wide author-phase cure is CONFIRMED exactly as ordered — tools\normalize_hebrew_in_json.py --write re-splice plus collate re-proof at byte tier, one pass. The 23-quote digit is CONFIRMED. The ROW ENUMERATION IS CORRECTED: the 23 runs sit in THIRTEEN rows, P05-001..P05-013, not eleven; P05-001..P05-011 account for only 20 of them.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived with the shipped tool, not by inspection. tools\normalize_hebrew_in_json.py dry-run over SP\Isa\draft_rows_combined.jsonl returns exactly {ok 392, fixed 23, mention 8, defect_count 0}, matching the standing validator report's hebrew_normalize_dryrun section digit for digit. So the class digit of 23 is right, and — the material point for the cure — there are ZERO hard defects: every affected run is canonically equivalent to a source window, so all 23 re-splice deterministically and none needs authorial judgement. PER-ROW ATTRIBUTION, run with the same tool logic per row and per field: all 23 runs sit in boundary_rationale, all sit in P05 rows, and they distribute as P05-001 (1), P05-002 (2), P05-003 (3), P05-004 (1), P05-005 (3), P05-006 (1), P05-007 (1), P05-008 (2), P05-009 (2), P05-010 (2), P05-011 (2), P05-012 (1), P05-013 (2). The docketed eleven sum to 20; P05-012 and P05-013 carry the remaining 3. BOTH UNLISTED ROWS ARE INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED AS CLASS MEMBERS BY THEIR OWN PEER RULINGS, so this is an enumeration gap and not a new class: peer_05.json P05-012 (refine, medium) remedy item (3) orders 're-splice the header run from source bytes; test = byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.13, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean'; peer_05.json P05-013 (uphold, medium) remedy item (1) orders 're-splice both pointed runs from source bytes ... byte collation returns byte at oshb:Isa.21.16 and oshb:Isa.21.17, Hebrew-normalization dry-run clean'. Same cure, same test, same class. CLASS BOUNDARY VERIFIED: no row outside P05 carries an NFD-degraded run anywhere in the corpus, and no field other than boundary_rationale is affected. So the class boundary is correct and only its row list was short. WHY IT PERSISTED: the normalize dry-run exits 0 on a non-zero 'fixed' count — a re-splice need is not a hard failure — so the standing validator report carries fixed=23 under hard_status GREEN. The count has to be read, not just the status.

consequence.spec: ONE deterministic author pass over all THIRTEEN rows; boundary_rationale only; no span, unit_type, parent, confidence or signal changes from this disposition. (1) Run tools\normalize_hebrew_in_json.py --write over the author-wave rows file. All 23 runs are canonically equivalent to source windows and are replaced with the source's exact bytes content-preservingly; no run requires re-wording and none may be hand-typed. Expected effect by row: P05-001 (1 run), P05-002 (2), P05-003 (3), P05-004 (1), P05-005 (3), P05-006 (1), P05-007 (1), P05-008 (2), P05-009 (2), P05-010 (2), P05-011 (2), P05-012 (1), P05-013 (2) — 23 total. (2) Collate re-proof at BYTE tier: after the re-splice, every pointed run in each of the thirteen rows is re-collated against its own cited verse with tools\collate.py and must return tier 'byte'. Any run returning accent_stripped, skeleton or none is a failure of the pass, not a tier to be disclosed. (3) The per-row tests the peers ordered ride along in the SAME pass and are not superseded by this class cure — in particular the named byte-collation targets oshb:Isa.21.11 (P05-011), oshb:Isa.21.13 (P05-012) and oshb:Isa.21.16 with oshb:Isa.21.17 (P05-013), and every other row's own peer remedy in peer_04.json, peer_04_r2.json and peer_05.json. Those remedies carry substantive repairs (tier labels, mark positions, digit objects) that the re-splice does not touch. (4) P05-005 and P05-009 are ALSO members of the whole-chapter class ruled at B-6 (Isa.18.1-Isa.18.7 and Isa.20.1-Isa.20.6). Their confidence/machinery treatment there and their re-splice here are independent and must both land. rulings.docket_item: CALIBRATION RECORD: the phase-wide lens asymmetry (primaries LF 155 support / 70 challenge vs OL 30 support / 195 challenge) as adjudicated by the peer wave (202 rulings = 124 uphold / 76 refine / 2 refute / 0 escalations).
rulings.decision: RECORDED for the mesh ledger, with one narrow cure and NO wholesale discount of either lens. The per-row adjudication does not support treating OL's challenge volume as register noise; it supports treating OL's SEVERITY AND TIER LABELS as inflated at the low end; and it exposes that the genuinely unaudited half of the asymmetry is LF's SUPPORT column, not its challenge column.
rulings.grounds: Every digit below is re-derived from the packets and peer files, not carried from the brief. PRIMARIES, re-counted over the 58 cluster packets (29 clusters x 2 lenses, 225 items each): LF 155 support / 70 challenge; OL 30 support / 195 challenge — confirmed exactly. Challenge severity AS FILED: LF 10 high / 43 medium / 17 low; OL 15 high / 129 medium / 51 low. PEER WAVE, re-counted over the 29 peer files: 202 rulings over 202 DISTINCT rows — one ruling per row, no row double-ruled — 124 uphold / 76 refine / 2 refute / 0 escalate; confirmed exactly. By source: OL-only 132 rulings (84 uphold, 47 refine, 1 refute); convergent 'both' 63 rulings (35 uphold, 28 refine, 0 refute); LF-only 7 rulings (5 uphold, 1 refine, 1 refute). Peer-recorded new_findings total 125; supported_sample entries total 3. WHAT THE PER-ROW ADJUDICATION ACTUALLY SHOWS. (a) OL's volume is not noise. 131 of 132 OL-only items survived as uphold or refine and exactly ONE was refuted — a 2.8-times higher challenge rate that produced findings which held on the bytes. Any wholesale discount of OL is refuted by its own refutation rate. (b) The inflation OL does carry is register-level, and it shows in the REFINE band and in severity, not in refutation. 76 of 202 rulings (37.6%) refined — defect real, framing or severity wrong — and the refine rate is HIGHEST on convergent rows (28 of 63, 44.4%) where both lenses pressed the same row, which is where over-claim is easiest and where the two framings most often turned out to be distinct defects rather than one. Severity moved down at the BOTTOM, not the top: OL filed 26.2% of its challenges low (51/195) and the peer wave finalized 40.2% low on OL-sourced items (53/132), while the high band barely moved (7.7% filed against 6.8% final). So the correction was medium-to-low re-banding, not challenge-to-refute. (c) THE UNAUDITED HALF IS LF'S SUPPORT COLUMN. Only 7 LF-only challenges reached peer adjudication at all — too few to characterise a lens from — and LF's 155 supports drew a verified sample of THREE rows across the entire wave (supported_sample entries = 3, 1.9% of 155). There is therefore no evidential basis for calling LF lax, and almost none for calling its supports verified. The asymmetry in the ledger is, at bottom, a COVERAGE fact about what was examined, not a reliability verdict about either lens. (d) Zero of 202 rulings escalated: no peer found an owner-level policy genuinely contested anywhere in the book. And the 125 peer-recorded new findings exceed the 76 refines, so BOTH packets under-covered the rows independently of lens — which is a fact about packet depth, not about lens bias. (e) Consistency check on this docket itself: of the five boundary items ruled here, two declined the challenging reading (B-1, B-4) and three adopted it (B-2, B-3, B-5), and the adoptions turned on byte-tier or tier-1 evidence while the declines turned on skeleton-tier evidence failing to beat a tier-1 signal. Neither lens's provenance predicted the outcome; the tier of the evidence did.
